chunks: And al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khalq ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Is-haq ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

The khuntha (hermaphrodite) is inherited from where they urinate; if they urinate from both, then from whichever one's urine precedes, they are inherited from it; if they die and have not urinated, then half the 'aql (bride price/dowry) of the woman and half the 'aql of the man.

key_terms.اَلْخُنْثَى: Hermaphrodite or person of ambiguous gender
key_terms.عَقْل: Bride price or dowry (used here to denote the share/value associated with gender)

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance calculated for a person of ambiguous gender (khuntha) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam establishes the juristic principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) and physical evidence to resolve gender ambiguity in inheritance shares. It highlights the Shia scholarly reliance on the preeminence of the urinary organ as the primary indicator of gender, ensuring precise allocation of the 'aql (blood money) when biological markers are indistinct. This ruling reflects the practical application of fiqh in managing complex familial estates during the early Imams' era.
